newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ EQUITIES WEATHER RISING RATES TO END SQUARE.
newsitem.headline: NZ EQUITIES WEATHER RISING RATES TO END SQUARE.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices pick up ground to end flat
* Equities take more note of lower dollar than higher rates
* Fletcher Energy actively traded, boosts turnover
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -1.29 at 2,538.45
363 -7 * NZSC cap index +1.66 at 5,281.92
343 -2 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +8.08 at 2,038.35
404 -1 * Volume NZ$86 million. Futures -9 at 1276
766 +3 * Other movers - +7, +6
New Zealand's equity market shrugged off another sharp rise in short term interest rates on Friday, preferring to focus on the falling kiwi dollar instead, allowing the market to end square.
Brokers said direction would be set by reports on future profitability from the larger companies as the reporting season proceeded.
"Generally, the market has mostly been awaiting the latest round of profit results to start giving a bit of direction," said Doyle Paterson Brown broker Murray Doyle.
The top 40 index closed just 1.29 points down at 2,538.45, picking up 10 points from its intraday low.
Telecom's three cent rise to $7.66 prevented the index falling too far. This was despite 90-day bank bills rising 17 basis points.

Turnover of $86 million was boosted by 6.8 million Fletcher Energy shares traded. The energy stock closed seven cents up at $5.52 as it responded to the rise in the value of its U.S. dollar-denominated assets. Brokers said Brierley Investments could be unloading the rest of its holding.
The Warehouse rose six cents to $4.80 after the discount retailer reported a 22.8 percent lift in fourth quarter sales.
Although Carter Holt Harvey expressed confidence about the future outlook after reporting on Thursday, its price slipped seven cents to $3.63.
Steel & Tube gained 15 cents to $7.50 and was typical of a number of stocks seen benefiting from the 11 percent fall in the New Zealand dollar since late last year.
